92.t:
He emigrated to Abyssinia.
His son ʿAbd Allāh said: When my father died, Ibn Masʿūd wept and said:
My brother and my companion with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the dearest of people to me, except for what happened with ʿUmar (2).
It is said: When he died, ʿUmar waited for Umm ʿAbd, so she came and prayed over him (3).
al-Zuhrī said: Ibn Masʿūd is not higher in our estimation than his brother ʿUtbah (4).
I say: His son ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah met the Prophet, had companionship and narrated a hadith, and he is the father of one of the seven jurists (الفقيه): ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah. ⟦1:500⟧

93.t:
- Khubayb ibn Yasāf * ibn ʿUnbah (1) ibn ʿAmr al-Anṣārī ibn Khadīj ibn ʿĀmir ibn Jusham ibn al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj al-Anṣārī, al-Khazrajī.
He had children: Abū Kathīr ʿAbd Allāh, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and Unaysah.
Jamīlah, daughter of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn (2) Salūl, was his wife, and his line has died out.
Ibn Saʿd: أنبأنا يزيد بن هارون، أنبأنا مستلم (3) بن سعيد، حدثنا خبيب بن عبد الرحمن بن خبيب بن يساف، عن أبيه، عن جده، قال:
I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he intended to go on an expedition, I and a man from my people who had not become Muslim.
We said: We are ashamed that our people should witness a battle that we do not witness.
He said: “Have you both become Muslim?”
We said: No.
He said: “We do not seek help from the polytheists against the polytheists (4).”
He said: So we became Muslim and witnessed it with him. I killed a man, and he struck me a blow. Afterwards I married his daughter, and she used to say to me: May you never lack a man whom this sash adorned for you.
I would say to her: May you never lack a man who hastened your father to the Fire (5).
Maʿn: حدثنا مالك، عن الفضيل بن أبي عبد الله، عن عبد الله بن نيار، عن عروة، عن عائشة، قالت:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out for Badr, and when he was at Ḥarrat al-Wabarah, a man overtook him of whom boldness and courage were mentioned, and they were glad of him.
She said: He said: I have come ⟦1:501⟧ to follow you and to share in what you gain.
The Prophet ﷺ said to him: “Do you believe in Allah and His Messenger?”
He said: No.
He said: “Then go back, for we will not seek help from a polytheist.”
Then he overtook him at al-Shajarah and said the same as he had said.
Then he overtook him at al-Baydāʾ, and he said: “Do you believe in Allah and His Messenger?”
He said: Yes.
He said: “Go forward (1).”
al-Wāqidī said: He is Khubayb ibn Yasāf. His acceptance of Islam was delayed until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out for Badr; he caught up with him, became Muslim, and witnessed Badr and Uḥud.
He said: He died in the caliphate (الخلافة) of ʿUthmān, and his offspring have died out (2).
It is said of his father: Isāf ibn ʿAdī.
Thus Ibn Abī Ḥātim named him.
Our shaykh al-Dimyāṭī (3) said: He is the one who killed Abū ʿUqbah al-Ḥārith ibn ʿĀmir.
So our shaykh said, and he judged mistaken what is in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī about the killing of Khubayb ibn ʿAdī the martyr, namely that he killed al-Ḥārith on the day of Badr, and so the family of al-Ḥārith killed him when they had taken him captive for it.
That is Khubayb ibn ʿAdī ibn Mālik of the Aws, and I did not find him mentioned among the Badrīs (البدري) (may Allah be pleased with him). ⟦1:502⟧

94.h: 90 - ʿUwaym ibn Sāʿidah ibn ʿĀʾish ibn Qays al-Anṣārī *
94.t:
ibn al-Nuʿmān ibn Zayd ibn Umayyah, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Anṣārī, of the Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf.
A leading Badrī (البدري), he witnessed the two ʿAqabahs according to al-Wāqidī, and he witnessed the second without dispute, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ paired him in brotherhood with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.
Ibn Isḥāq said: Rather, between him and Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿah (1).
Mūsā ibn Yaʿqūb al-Zamʿī: عن السري بن عبد الرحمن، عن عباد بن حمزة، سمع جابرا:
He heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “What an excellent servant among the servants of Allah, and a man of the people of Paradise: ʿUwaym ibn Sāʿidah (2).”
It is said: He was the first to cleanse himself with water after relieving himself.
Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān: عن ابن شهاب، عن عبيد الله بن عبد الله، عن ابن عباس:
The two righteous men who met Abū Bakr and ʿUmar as they were heading for the portico ⟦1:503⟧ of the Banū Sāʿidah, mentioned what the people had conspired upon, and said: Where are you going?
They said: We want our brothers from the Anṣār.
They said: There is no harm if you do not approach them; settle your affair.
Ibn Shihāb said: ʿUrwah informed me that the two were: ʿUwaym ibn Sāʿidah and Maʿn ibn ʿAdī (1).
It is said: ʿUwaym is among those about whom was revealed: “In it are men who love to purify themselves (2)” [Qurʾān 9:108].
Ibn Saʿd said: ʿUwaym ibn Sāʿidah died in the caliphate (الخلافة) of ʿUmar, aged 65 (3).
I say: It is said that he was originally of Balī. ⟦1:504⟧

96.h: 1 - ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit ibn Qays ibn Aṣram al-Anṣārī * (ع)
96.t:
ibn Qays ibn Aṣram ibn Fihr ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Ghanm ibn ʿAwf ibn [ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf] (1) ibn al-Khazraj.
The Imam (الإمام), the exemplar (القدوة), Abū al-Walīd al-Anṣārī, one of the leaders on the night of al-ʿAqabah, and among the notables of the Badrīs (البدري).
He settled in Jerusalem.
Narrating from him: أبو أمامة الباهلي، وأنس بن مالك، وأبو مسلم الخولاني الزاهد، وجبير بن نفير، وجنادة بن أبي أمية، وعبد الرحمن بن عسيلة الصنابحي، ومحمود بن الربيع، وأبو إدريس الخولاني، وأبو الأشعث الصنعاني، وابنه؛ الوليد بن عبادة، وأبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن، وخالد بن معدان - ولم يلحقاه، فهو مرسل - وابن زوجته؛ أبو أبي، وكثير بن مرة، وحطان بن عبد الله الرقاشي، وآخرون.
Ibn Isḥāq said, in listing those who witnessed the first ʿAqabah: ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit; he witnessed all the battles with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. ⟦2:5⟧
Muḥammad ibn Sābiq: حدثنا حشرج بن نباتة، عن موسى بن محمد بن إبراهيم التيمي، سمع أبا قلابة يقول:
حدثني الصنابحي: أن عبادة بن الصامت حدثه، قال:
I was alone with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: Which of your companions is dearest to you, that I may love him?
He said: “Keep it secret from me for as long as I live: Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, then ʿUmar, then ʿAlī.”
Then he fell silent, and I said: Then who, O Messenger of Allah?
He said: “Who could it be but al-Zubayr, Ṭalḥah, Saʿd, Abū ʿUbaydah, Muʿādh, Abū Ṭalḥah, Abū Ayyūb, and you, O ʿUbādah, and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, Abū al-Dardāʾ, Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAwf, Ibn ʿAffān, then this group of the clients (المولى): Salmān, Ṣuhayb, Bilāl, and ʿAmmār (1).”
Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī said: Five of the Anṣār collected the Qurʾān in the time of the Prophet ﷺ: Muʿādh, ʿUbādah, Ubayy, Abū Ayyūb, and Abū al-Dardāʾ.
When ʿUmar became ruler (2), Yazīd (3) ibn Abī Sufyān wrote to him:
The people of Syria are many, and they need someone to teach them the Qurʾān and give them understanding of the religion.
He said: Help me with three men.
They said: This one is a very old man - meaning Abū Ayyūb - and this one is ailing - meaning Ubayy.
So the three went out to Syria, and he said: Begin with Homs, and when you are satisfied with them, let one go out to Damascus and another to Palestine (4). ⟦2:6⟧
Burd ibn Sinān: عن إسحاق بن قبيصة بن ذؤيب، عن أبيه:
ʿUbādah objected to something Muʿāwiyah did, and said: I will not live with you in one land.
So he travelled to Medina.
ʿUmar said to him: What brought you here?
He informed him of what Muʿāwiyah had done, and he said [to him] (1): Go back to your place, for may Allah make hideous a land in which you and those like you are not present, and he has no authority over you (2).
Ibn Abī Uways: عن أبيه، عن الوليد بن داود بن محمد بن عبادة بن الصامت (3)، عن ابن عمه؛ عبادة بن الوليد، قال:
ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit was with Muʿāwiyah, and one day he gave the call to prayer, and a speaker stood up praising Muʿāwiyah and extolling him. ʿUbādah stood with dust in his hand and stuffed it into the speaker's mouth, and Muʿāwiyah became angry.
ʿUbādah said to him: You were not with us when we pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at al-ʿAqabah to hear and obey, in our energy and our reluctance, in our ease and our hardship, and when others are preferred over us, and not to dispute the matter with those entitled to it, and to stand for the truth wherever we were, fearing in Allah the blame of no one who blames. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When you see those who flatter, throw dust in their mouths” (4). ⟦2:7⟧
Yaḥyā al-Qaṭṭān: حدثنا ثور بن يزيد، حدثنا (1) مالك بن شرحبيل، قال:
ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit said: Do you not see that I cannot stand except with help (2), and I eat only what has been softened and warmed - and my companion died long ago - meaning his member - and it would not please me to be alone with a woman not lawful for me, even if I were given all that the sun shines upon, for fear that Satan would come and stir it, even though it has no hearing and no sight (3).
Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh: عن ابن خثيم، حدثنا إسماعيل بن عبيد بن ⟦2:8⟧ رفاعة، قال:
Muʿāwiyah wrote to ʿUthmān: ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit has corrupted Syria and its people for me, so either restrain him to yourself, or I will leave him and Syria to each other.
He wrote to him: Dispatch ʿUbādah until you return him to his home in Medina.
He said: He entered upon ʿUthmān, who was taken by surprise only when he found him with him in the house, and he turned to him and said: O ʿUbādah, what is between us and you?
ʿUbādah stood among the people and said:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “After me there will govern your affairs men who make known to you what you reject and reject what you know; so there is no obedience to one who disobeys, and do not go astray from your Lord (1).”
Yaḥyā ibn Sulaym: عن ابن خثيم، عن إسماعيل بن عبيد بن رفاعة، ⟦2:9⟧ عن أبيه:
A caravan (1) carrying wine passed by ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit - while he was in Syria - and he said: What is this? Is it oil?
It was said: No, it is wine being sold for so-and-so.
He took a blade from the market and went to it, and did not leave a single water-skin in it without slitting it - and Abū Hurayrah was then in Syria - so so-and-so sent to Abū Hurayrah and said: Will you not restrain your brother ʿUbādah from us? In the mornings he goes out to the market and spoils (2) the merchandise of the protected non-Muslims, and in the evenings he sits in the mosque with no work but to revile our honour and find fault with us!
He said: Abū Hurayrah came to him and said: O ʿUbādah, what is between you and Muʿāwiyah? Leave him and what he bears.
He said: You were not with us when we pledged allegiance to hear and obey, to enjoin the right and forbid the wrong, and that in Allah the blame of no one who blames would deter us.
Abū Hurayrah fell silent.
And so-and-so wrote to ʿUthmān: ʿUbādah has corrupted Syria for me (3).
al-Walīd ibn Muslim: حدثنا عثمان بن أبي العاتكة:
ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit passed by the village of Dummar (4) and ordered his servant to cut for him a toothstick from a willow on the River Baradā. He went to do so, then he said to him: Come back, for if it is not for a price, it will dry out and become firewood for a price.
وعن أبي حزرة يعقوب بن مجاهد، عن عبادة بن الوليد بن عبادة، عن أبيه، قال:
ʿUbādah was a tall, stout, handsome man.
He died in al-Ramlah in the year 34, aged 72. ⟦2:10⟧
Ibn Saʿd said: I heard someone say that he lived until he died in the time of Muʿāwiyah, in his caliphate (الخلافة) (1).
Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr and a group said: He died in the year 34.
Ḍamrah said, from Rajāʾ ibn Abī Salamah: The grave of ʿUbādah is in Jerusalem.
al-Haytham ibn ʿAdī said: He died in the year 45 (may Allah be pleased with him).
I say: Baqī included from him in his Musnad one hundred and eighty-one hadiths, and he has in al-Bukhārī and Muslim six.
al-Bukhārī alone has two, and Muslim two (2).

97.h: 2 - Abū Ḥudhāfah al-Sahmī ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥudhāfah ibn Qays * (س)
97.t:
ibn ʿAdī, Abū Ḥudhāfah al-Sahmī.
One of the foremost converts, he emigrated to Abyssinia, and the Prophet ﷺ dispatched him as a messenger to Khosrow (3).
He has a small amount of narration. ⟦2:11⟧
He went out to Syria as a fighter, and was taken captive at Caesarea; they brought him to their tyrant, who tried to draw him away from his religion, but he was not led astray.
Narrating from him: سليمان بن يسار، وأبو وائل، ومسعود بن الحكم، وأبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن.
al-Bukhārī said: His hadith is mursal (مرسل).
Abū Bakr ibn al-Barqī said: What was memorised from him is three hadiths that are not connected.
Abū Saʿīd ibn Yūnus and Ibn Mandah said: He witnessed Badr.
Yūnus: عن الزهري، عن أبي سلمة: that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥudhāfah stood to pray and recited aloud, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “O Ibn Ḥudhāfah! Do not make me hear, and let Allah hear (1).”
محمد بن عمرو: عن عمر بن الحكم بن ثوبان، أن أبا سعيد قال:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent out a detachment, with ʿAlqamah ibn Mujazziz over them, and I was among them.
We set out, and when we were part of the way along the road, a group asked his permission, and he permitted them, and appointed ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥudhāfah over them. He was one of the people of Badr, and he had a sense of humour. While we were on the road, the men lit a fire to warm themselves by it and to prepare a meal of theirs on it, when he said: Do I not have your hearing and obedience?
They said: Indeed.
He said: Then I command you by my right and your obedience to leap into this fire.
Some people stood up and girded themselves (2), ⟦2:12⟧ until, when he thought they were about to fall into it, he said: Hold back, I was only joking with you.
When they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ they mentioned that to him, and he said: “Whoever commands you to disobedience, do not obey him (1).”
Abū Yaʿlā included it in his Musnad.
Ibn al-Munkadir narrated it from ʿUmar ibn al-Ḥakam, and made it mursal (مرسل).
Thābit al-Bunānī narrated from Anas:
that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Ask me.”
A man said: Who is my father, O Messenger of Allah?
He said: “Your father is Ḥudhāfah” (2). ⟦2:13⟧
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muʿāwiyah al-Jumaḥī: حدثنا عبد العزيز القسملي، حدثنا ضرار بن عمرو، عن أبي رافع، قال:
ʿUmar sent an army to the Romans, and they captured ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥudhāfah and took him to their king, saying: This one is from the companions of Muḥammad.
He said: Would you convert to Christianity, and I will give you half of my kingdom?
He said: If you gave me all that you own and all the kingdom of the Arabs, I would not turn back from the religion of Muḥammad for the blink of an eye.
He said: Then I will kill you.
He said: You and that.
So he ordered him to be crucified, and said to the archers: Shoot near his body.
All the while he offered it to him and he refused. Then he took him down and called for a cauldron, into which water was poured until it boiled fiercely, and he called for two Muslim prisoners, ordered one of them, and he was thrown into it, while he offered Christianity to him and he refused, then he wept.
It was said to the king: He wept.
He thought that he had become anxious, and said: Bring him back.
What made you weep?
He said: I said: It is one soul that will be thrown in now and be gone, and I wished that I had as many souls as the hairs of my head to be thrown into the Fire for Allah.
The tyrant said to him: Would you kiss my head, and I will release you?
ʿAbd Allāh said to him: And all the prisoners?
He said: Yes.
So he kissed his head, and returned with the prisoners to ʿUmar and informed him of his account.
ʿUmar said: It is a duty upon every Muslim to kiss the head of Ibn Ḥudhāfah, and I will begin.
Then he kissed his head (1). ⟦2:14⟧
al-Walīd ibn Muslim: حدثنا أبو عمرو، ومالك بن أنس:
that the people of Caesarea captured Ibn Ḥudhāfah, and their king ordered that he be tested with various things, which he endured, then they placed him in a house with wine and pork for three days, and he did not eat.
They looked in on him, and said to the king:
His neck has bent; if you bring him out, well, otherwise he will die.
He brought him out and said: What kept you from eating and drinking?
He said: Necessity had made them lawful for me, but I disliked to give you cause to gloat over Islam.
He said: Then kiss my head, and I will free a hundred prisoners for you.
He said: As for this, yes.
He kissed his head, and he freed a hundred for him, and let him go.
Ibn ʿĀʾidh narrated the story of Ibn Ḥudhāfah, saying:
al-Walīd ibn Muḥammad narrated to us: that Ibn Ḥudhāfah was captured ..., then he mentioned the story at length, and in it he released three hundred prisoners for him, and gave him a reward of thirty thousand dinars, thirty maidservants and thirty manservants.
Perhaps this king had become Muslim in secret, and his excessive honouring of Ibn Ḥudhāfah indicates that.
The same is said of Heraclius when he proposed to his people entering the religion, and when he feared them he said:
I was only testing your firmness in your religion.
Whoever becomes Muslim inwardly in this way, deliverance from eternal abiding in the Fire is hoped for him, since some faith has come about in his inner self (1). What is feared is only that he has submitted to Islam and to the Messenger and believed that both are true, while remaining on a valid religion, so you see him revering both religions, as many nominal Muslims of the government bureaus have done (2); this does not benefit him ⟦2:15⟧ Islam until he disavows polytheism.
Ibn Ḥudhāfah died in the caliphate (الخلافة) of ʿUthmān - may Allah be pleased with them.

98.h: 3 - Abū Rāfiʿ, the client (المولى) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ * (ع)
98.t:
From the Copts of Egypt.
It is said: His name is Ibrāhīm.
It is said: Aslam.
He was a slave of al-ʿAbbās, who gave him to the Prophet ﷺ, and when the Prophet ﷺ was given the good news of al-ʿAbbās's conversion to Islam, he freed him.
He narrated a number of hadiths.
Narrating from him: his son ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Rāfiʿ, his grandson al-Faḍl ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, أبو سعيد المقبري، وعمرو بن الشريد، وجماعة كثيرة.
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn also narrated from him, though it seems he did not hear from him directly.
He witnessed the Battle of Uḥud and the Trench, and he was a man of knowledge and excellence.
He died in the caliphate (الخلافة) of ʿAlī.
It is said: He died in Kufa in the year 40 (may Allah be pleased with him).
It is said: He made a bequest to ʿAlī, and ʿAlī used to pay zakat on the property of the sons of Abū Rāfiʿ while they were orphans.
Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj said: I was informed that he was a Copt. ⟦2:16⟧
Shuʿbah: عن الحكم، عن ابن أبي رافع، عن أبيه:
that the Prophet ﷺ sent a man to collect charity, and he said to Abū Rāfiʿ: Come with me, and we will take a share of it.
I said: Not until I ask permission of the Messenger of Allah.
So I asked his permission, and he said: “O Abū Rāfiʿ, the client (المولى) of a people is one of them, and charity is not lawful for us (1).”
Sulaymān ibn Yasār said:
Abū Rāfiʿ said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not order me to stop at al-Abṭaḥ when he left Minā, but I came and stopped, and he came and stopped (2).

99.h: 4 - Ṣuhayb ibn Sinān Abū Yaḥyā al-Namarī * (ع)
99.t:
Of al-Namir ibn Qāsiṭ.
He is known as al-Rūmī because he stayed among the Romans for a time.
He was from the people of al-Jazīrah, taken captive from the village of Nineveh, in the districts of ⟦2:17⟧ Mosul.
His father or his uncle had been an agent of Khosrow, then he was brought to Mecca, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Judʿān al-Qurashī al-Taymī bought him.
It is said: Rather, he fled and came to Mecca and made a pact of alliance with Ibn Judʿān.
He was among the great foremost converts and the Badrīs (البدري).
Narrating from him: بنوه؛ حبيب، وزياد (1)، وحمزة؛ وسعيد بن المسيب، وكعب الحبر، وعبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى، وآخرون.
He narrated a limited number of hadiths, which they included for him in the Six Books (الكتب الستة).
He was a man of excellence, held in great esteem, and had several children.
When ʿUmar was stabbed, he appointed him to lead the Muslims in prayer until the people of the Council agreed upon an imam.
He was described as generous and open-handed (may Allah be pleased with him).
He died in Medina, in Shawwāl, in the year 38, and he was among those who withdrew from the strife and attended to his own affairs (may Allah be pleased with him).
The hadith master (الحافظ) Ibn ʿAsākir said: Ṣuhayb ibn Sinān ibn Mālik ibn ʿAbd (2) ʿAmr ibn ʿUqayl ibn ʿĀmir, Abū Yaḥyā - and it is said Abū Ghassān - al-Namarī, al-Rūmī, al-Badrī, al-Muhājirī.
Narrating from him: بنوه، وابن عمر، وجابر، وابن المسيب، وعبيد بن عمير، وابن أبي ليلى، وبنوه الثمانية: عثمان، وصيفي، وحمزة، وسعد، وعباد، وحبيب، وصالح، ومحمد. ⟦2:18⟧
Ibn Saʿd mentioned him and listed his lineage up to Aslam ibn Aws Manāh ibn al-Namir ibn Qāsiṭ, of Rabīʿah, confederate of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Judʿān al-Taymī al-Qurashī.
His mother was Salmā bint Qaʿīd.
He was a reddish man, very red, not tall.
Shabāb (1) mentioned his lineage up to al-Namir, with additional forefathers and others omitted.
Aḥmad ibn al-Barqī did likewise.
From Ḥamzah ibn Ṣuhayb, from his father, who said:
The Prophet ﷺ gave me the patronymic (الكنية) Abū Yaḥyā (2).
From Ṣayfī ibn Ṣuhayb, from his father, who said:
I accompanied the Prophet ﷺ before revelation came to him (3).
And from Abū ʿUbaydah ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAmmār, from his father:
ʿAmmār said: I met Ṣuhayb at the door of the house of al-Arqam, in which was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so we entered, and he presented Islam to us, and we became Muslim, then we remained so for a day until evening came, and we left while hiding (4).
Yūnus narrated, from al-Ḥasan:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Ṣuhayb is the foremost of the Romans” (5). ⟦2:19⟧
This came with a good chain of transmission (الإسناد) from the hadith of Abū Umāmah, and it came from the hadith of Anas and Umm Hāniʾ (1).
Mujāhid said: The first to make Islam public were seven: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr, Bilāl, Khabbāb, Ṣuhayb ..., abridged (2).
Abū ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: The father of Ṣuhayb, or his uncle, was an agent of Khosrow over al-Ubullah, and their dwellings were in the land of Mosul (3), and the Romans raided them and took Ṣuhayb captive while he was a boy, so he grew up among the Romans, then Kalb bought him, and they sold him in Mecca to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Judʿān, who freed him.
As for his family, they claim that he fled from the Romans and came to Mecca (4).
Muṣʿab ibn ʿAbd Allāh: عن أبيه، عن ربيعة بن عثمان، عن زيد بن أسلم، عن أبيه، قال:
I went out with ʿUmar until he entered an orchard of Ṣuhayb.
When Ṣuhayb saw him, he said: O people! O folk!
ʿUmar said: Why does he call to the people?
I said: Rather, it is a servant of his called Yuḥannas (5).
ʿUmar said to him: Were it not for three traits in you, O ⟦2:20⟧
Ṣuhayb ..., the hadith (1).
al-Wāqidī: حدثنا عثمان بن محمد، عن عبد الحكم بن صهيب، عن عمر بن الحكم، قال:
ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir was tortured until he did not know what he was saying, and Ṣuhayb was tortured until he did not know what he was saying, among a group of Muslims, until was revealed: “Then indeed your Lord, for those who emigrated after they had been persecuted” [Qurʾān 16:110] (2).
Mujāhid said: As for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, his uncle protected him, and as for Abū Bakr, his people protected him, and the others were seized - he named Ṣuhayb among them - and they dressed them in iron coats of mail and scorched them in the sun until the hardship reached them to the utmost; so they gave them what they asked - meaning: uttering disbelief - and every man's people came with leather mats containing water, and threw them in it, except Bilāl. ⟦2:21⟧
al-Kalbī: from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: “And among the people is he who sells himself ...” [Qurʾān 2:207] was revealed about Ṣuhayb and a group of his companions, whom the people of Mecca seized to torture them in order to turn them back to polytheism (1).
Aḥmad in his Musnad: حدثنا أسباط، حدثنا أشعث، عن كردوس، عن ابن مسعود، قال:
The nobles of Quraysh passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while Khabbāb, Ṣuhayb, Bilāl, and ʿAmmār were with him, and they said: Are you content with these?
Then the Qurʾān was revealed about them: “And warn by it those who fear ...” up to His saying: “and Allah is most knowing of the wrongdoers” [Qurʾān 6 (2): 51 - 58].
ʿAwf al-Aʿrābī: from Abū ʿUthmān:
that when Ṣuhayb wanted to emigrate, the people of Mecca said to him: You came to us a poor, insignificant man, and your condition has changed!
He said: What do you think if I leave my wealth, will you let me go on my way?
They said: Yes.
So he handed his wealth over to them.
That reached the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “Ṣuhayb has profited! Ṣuhayb has profited!” (3).
Yaʿqūb ibn Muḥammad al-Zuhrī: حدثنا حصين بن حذيفة (4) بن صيفي، حدثنا ⟦2:22⟧ أبي وعمومتي، عن سعيد بن المسيب، عن صهيب، قال:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I was shown the abode of your emigration, a salt marsh between two lava fields! It is either Hajar or Yathrib (1).”
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out for Medina, and I had intended (2) to go out with him, but some young men of Quraysh prevented me, so that night I kept standing up and not sitting down.
They said: Allah has occupied him from you with his stomach - and I was not ill - so they slept, and I went, but some of them caught up with me at a distance of a postal stage.
I said to them: Shall I give you several ounces of gold and you let me go?
They did so, and I said: Dig under the threshold of the door (3), you will find it, and take from so-and-so two robes.
I went out until I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Qubāʾ, and when he saw me, he said: “O Abū Yaḥyā, the sale has profited,” three times.
I said: None informed you but Gabriel.
Ḥammād ibn Salamah: حدثنا علي بن زيد، عن ابن المسيب، قال:
Ṣuhayb came as an emigrant, and a group followed him, so he dismounted from his mount and emptied his quiver, and said:
You know that I am among the best of you in archery, and by Allah, you will not reach me until I have shot every arrow I have, then I strike you with my sword; but if you wish, I will show you where my wealth is, and you will let me go on my way?
They said: We will.
When he came to the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The sale has profited, O Abū Yaḥyā!”, and was revealed: “And among the people is he who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah” [Qurʾān 2:207] (4). ⟦2:23⟧
Muṣʿab al-Zubayrī said: Ṣuhayb fled from the Romans with wealth and settled in Mecca, and made a pact with Ibn Judʿān; the Romans had taken him only from Nineveh.
ʿAbd al-Ḥakīm ibn Ṣuhayb: عن عمر بن الحكم بن ثوبان، عن صهيب، قال:
I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Qubāʾ, having developed sore eyes on the way and being hungry, and in front of him were fresh dates, and I fell upon them.
ʿUmar said: O Messenger of Allah! Do you not see Ṣuhayb eating dates while he has sore eyes?
The Prophet ﷺ said that to me.
I said: I am only eating on the side of my healthy eye, and he smiled (1).
ʿUrwah, Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah and others mentioned Ṣuhayb among those who witnessed Badr.
Abū Zurʿah: حدثنا يوسف بن عدي، حدثنا يوسف بن محمد بن يزيد بن صيفي، عن أبيه، عن جده، عن أبي جده، عن صهيب:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him love Ṣuhayb with the love of a mother for her child (2).”
Ḥammād ibn Salamah: عن ثابت، عن معاوية بن قرة، عن عائذ بن عمرو: that ⟦2:24⟧ Salmān, Ṣuhayb, and Bilāl were sitting, and Abū Sufyān passed by them, and they said:
The swords of Allah have not yet taken their due from the neck of the enemy of Allah.
Abū Bakr said: Do you say this to the elder of Quraysh and its master?
He said: The Prophet ﷺ was informed of that and said: “O Abū Bakr, perhaps you have angered them; if you have angered them, you have angered your Lord.”
So he went back to them and said: O my brothers, perhaps you are angry?
They said: No, O Abū Bakr, may Allah forgive you (1).
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAqīl: عن حمزة بن صهيب، عن أبيه، قال:
ʿUmar said to Ṣuhayb: What a man you are, were it not for three traits in you!
He said: And what are they?
He said: You took a patronymic (الكنية) though you have no child, you claimed descent from the Arabs though you are of the Romans! And there is extravagance in you with food.
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave me the patronymic (الكنية) Abū Yaḥyā, and I am of al-Namir ibn Qāsiṭ; the Romans took me captive from Mosul after I was a boy who knew my lineage; and as for what you said about extravagance with food:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “The best of you is he who feeds food (2).”
And Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAlqamah narrated: عن يحيى بن عبد الرحمن بن حاطب، عن أبيه:
that ʿUmar said to Ṣuhayb: Were it not for three in you?
Some narrate it omitting: “from his father.”
And he added: Even if a piece of dung (3) were split open for me, I would claim descent to it.
And Ḥammād ibn Salamah: عن زيد بن أسلم:
that ʿUmar said to Ṣuhayb: Were it not for three ⟦2:25⟧ traits.
He said: And what are they? By Allah, you never stop finding fault with something.
He said: Your taking a patronymic (الكنية) though you have no child; your claiming descent to al-Namir ibn Qāsiṭ though you are a man with a foreign accent (1); and that you do not hold on to wealth ..., the hadith.
And in it: And a wet nurse was sought for me in al-Ubullah (2), so this is from that.
As for wealth, do you see me spend except in what is right?
And Sālim narrated, from his father:
that ʿUmar said: If something befalls me, let Ṣuhayb lead the people in prayer - three times - then agree upon your affair on the third day.
al-Wāqidī said: Ṣuhayb died in Medina, in Shawwāl, in the year 38, aged 70.
So too said al-Madāʾinī and others about his death.
al-Madāʾinī said: He lived 73 years.
al-Fasawī said: He lived 84 years (may Allah be pleased with him).
He has about thirty hadiths.
Muslim narrated three of them from him (3). ⟦2:26⟧

100.h: 5 - Abū Ṭalḥah al-Anṣārī Zayd ibn Sahl ibn al-Aswad * (ع)
100.t:
A companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and of the Banū of his maternal uncles, one of the notables of the Badrīs (البدري), and one of the twelve leaders on the night of al-ʿAqabah.
His name is Zayd ibn Sahl ibn al-Aswad ibn Ḥarām ibn ʿAmr ibn Zayd Manāh ibn ʿAdī ibn ʿAmr ibn Mālik ibn al-Najjār al-Khazrajī, al-Najjārī.
He has hadiths.
Narrating from him: ربيبه؛ أنس بن مالك، وزيد بن خالد الجهني، وابن عباس، وابنه؛ أبو إسحاق عبد الله بن أبي طلحة.
He had fasted continuously after the Prophet (1) ﷺ.
He is the one who saw no harm in the fasting person swallowing hail, and would say: It is neither food nor drink (2). ⟦2:27⟧
He is the one about whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The voice of Abū Ṭalḥah in the army is better than a troop (1).”
His merits are many.
It is said: He fought on the Roman Sea and died on the ship.
The better known is that he died in Medina and ʿUthmān prayed over him in the year 34 (may Allah be pleased with him).
Ibn Abī ʿArūbah: عن قتادة، عن أنس:
Abū Ṭalḥah, Muʿādh, and Abū ʿUbaydah used to drink ṭilāʾ in Syria, that which was cooked down to a third, two-thirds having gone (2).
I say: It is dibs.
ʿUrwah, Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah, and Ibn Isḥāq mentioned:
that Abū Ṭalḥah was among those who witnessed al-ʿAqabah and Badr. ⟦2:28⟧
Abū Zurʿah al-Dimashqī said: Abū Ṭalḥah lived forty years after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, fasting continuously (1).
I say: Rather, he lived after him some twenty-odd years.
Aḥmad ibn al-Barqī said: Abū Ṭalḥah was a Badrī (البدري), a leader; ʿUthmān prayed over him; about twenty hadiths came from him.
Ḥammād ibn Salamah: عن ثابت، وعلي بن زيد، عن أنس:
that his sons said to Abū Ṭalḥah: You have fought in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, so we will fight on your behalf.
He refused, and fought at sea, and died (2).
Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān: عن ثابت، عن أنس، قال:
Abū Ṭalḥah proposed to Umm Sulaym, and she said:
I do desire you, and one like you is not turned away, but you are an unbeliever; if you become Muslim, that is my dowry, and I ask nothing else of you.
So he became Muslim and married her.
Thābit said: We never heard of a dowry more noble than the dowry of Umm Sulaym: Islam (3).
al-Ṭayālisī: حدثنا سليمان بن المغيرة، وحماد، وجعفر بن سليمان، عن ثابت، عن أنس، قال أبو داود:
وحدثناه شيخ سمعه من النضر بن ⟦2:29⟧ أنس:
Mālik - the father of Anas - said to his wife: I see that this man forbids wine.
He went off until he reached Syria, and perished there.
Then Abū Ṭalḥah came proposing to Umm Sulaym, and she said: One like you is not turned away, but you are an unbelieving man, and I want no dowry but Islam.
He said: Who will arrange that for me?
She said: The Prophet ﷺ.
He went off seeking him, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “Abū Ṭalḥah has come to you with the radiance of Islam between his eyes.”
He said: So he married her on that basis ..., the hadith at length, and how his son by her died, and she concealed it from him and adorned herself for him until he had relations with her, then she informed him, and said:
Allah had lent you a loan, and He took it back, so seek reward for your son (1).
Anas said:
Abū Ṭalḥah said: The sword fell from me on the day of Badr, because of the drowsiness that overcame us (2).
Ḥammād ibn Salamah: عن ثابت، عن أنس:
that Abū Ṭalḥah fasted for forty years after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, breaking his fast only on the day of Fiṭr or Aḍḥā.
Gharīb (الغريب), meeting the condition of Muslim (3). ⟦2:30⟧
And by it: that Abū Ṭalḥah said: I will not take command over two, nor will I blame them (1).
Thābit narrated from Anas:
that Abū Ṭalḥah used to shoot in front of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Uḥud, and he was a skilled archer.
When Abū Ṭalḥah shot, the Messenger of Allah would raise his sight to see where his arrow fell.
And he would push the chest of the Messenger of Allah with his hand, and say:
O Messenger of Allah, like this, so that no arrow strikes you (2).
ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Ṣuhayb narrated from Anas, who said:
On the day of Uḥud, some people fled from the Messenger of Allah, while Abū Ṭalḥah was in front of him, shielding him with a small shield.
He was a skilled archer with a strong draw, and he broke two or three bows that day.
A man would pass by with a quiver of arrows, and he ﷺ would say: “Scatter them for Abū Ṭalḥah.”
Then he would peer toward the enemy, and Abū Ṭalḥah would say: O Prophet of Allah, may my father be your ransom, do not peer out, lest an arrow strike you, my neck before your neck.
He said: I saw ʿĀʾishah and Umm Sulaym, with their garments tucked up (3), I could see the anklets on their legs, as the two of them hurried, with the water-skins on their backs, pouring them into the mouths of the men, then returning and filling them again.
The sword fell from the hand of Abū Ṭalḥah two or three times from drowsiness (4). ⟦2:31⟧
Ibn ʿUyaynah: حدثنا علي بن زيد، عن أنس:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say: “The voice of Abū Ṭalḥah in the army is better than a troop (1).”
And when he remained with the Prophet ﷺ, he would kneel in front of him and say:
My soul be a ransom for your soul, and my face a shield for your face (2).
Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated from Thābit, from Anas, who said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The voice of Abū Ṭalḥah is harder on the polytheists than a troop.”
al-Thawrī: عن عبد الله بن محمد بن عقيل، عن جابر - أو أنس - قال:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The voice of Abū Ṭalḥah in the army is better than a thousand men” (3).
Ḥammād ibn Salamah: عن إسحاق بن عبد الله بن أبي طلحة، عن أنس:
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of Ḥunayn: “Whoever kills an enemy has his spoils.”
Abū Ṭalḥah killed twenty men that day and took their spoils (4).
هشام: عن ابن سيرين، عن أنس:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sacrificed and had his head shaved, and he handed the barber his right side, and he shaved it, then he called Abū Ṭalḥah and gave it to him, then ⟦2:32⟧ he handed him his left side, and said: “Shave,” and gave it to Abū Ṭalḥah, who distributed it among the people (1).
Ibn ʿAwn narrated it from Muḥammad (2), and made it mursal (مرسل).
Anas said: Abū Ṭalḥah was the wealthiest of the Anṣār in Medina in palm groves, and he said:
O Messenger of Allah, the dearest of my properties to me is Bayruḥāʾ, and it is a charity for Allah; I hope for its righteousness and its store, so place it, O Messenger of Allah, where Allah shows you.
He said: “Excellent! That is profitable property, and I think you should put it among the relatives (3).”
Ḥumayd narrated from Anas, who said:
After the Prophet ﷺ, Abū Ṭalḥah did not break his fast except on a journey or in illness (4).
Qatādah and Ḥumayd narrated from Anas:
Abū Ṭalḥah used to eat hail while fasting, and say: It is neither food nor drink, it is only a blessing.
ʿAlī ibn Judʿān alone narrated it in this form ⟦2:33⟧ from Anas: and I informed the Messenger of Allah, and he said: “Take from your uncle (1).”
Ḥammād ibn Salamah: عن ثابت، وعلي بن زيد، عن أنس:
that Abū Ṭalḥah recited: “March forth, light and heavy” [Qurʾān 9:42], and said:
Allah has called us to march and has commanded us, our elders and our youths, so equip me.
His sons said: May Allah have mercy on you! You fought in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, and we will fight on your behalf now.
He said: So he fought at sea and died, and they found no island to bury him in except after seven days, and he had not changed (2).
He died in the year 34.
Khalīfah alone said: in the year 32.
The hadith master (الحافظ) Abū Muḥammad told us: The Prophet ﷺ shaved one side of his head and distributed it among the people, then shaved his other side and gave it to Abū Ṭalḥah (3).
He said: He was tough, loud-voiced, dark-complexioned, of medium height, and his grey hair did not change colour.
ʿUthmān prayed over him.
It is said: He died in the year 51.
He narrated from the Prophet ﷺ twenty-odd hadiths, of which two are in the two Ṣaḥīḥs (الصحيحين).
al-Bukhārī alone has one hadith, and Muslim one (4). ⟦2:34⟧

101.h: 6 - Abū Burdah ibn Niyār ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd al-Balawī * (ع)
101.t:
ibn ʿAmr ibn Kilāb ibn Dahmān al-Balawī, al-Quḍāʿī, al-Anṣārī, of the confederates of the Aws.
His name is Hāniʾ.
He is the maternal uncle of al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib (1).
He witnessed al-ʿAqabah, Badr, and the Prophet's battles.
He lived on into the reign of Muʿāwiyah.
His hadith is in the Six Books (الكتب الستة).
Narrating from him: ابن أخته البراء، وجابر بن عبد الله، وبشير بن يسار، وغيرهم. ⟦2:35⟧
He was one of the described archers.
It is said: He died in the year 42.

102.h: 7 - Jabr ibn ʿAtīk ibn Qays ibn Hayshah ibn al-Ḥārith al-Anṣārī *
102.t:
ibn Umayyah ibn Muʿāwiyah ibn Mālik ibn ʿAwf ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf al-Anṣārī, Abū ʿAbd Allāh.
A leading Badrī (البدري).
It is said: His name is Jābir.
He had children: ʿAtīk, ʿAbd Allāh, and Umm Thābit.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ paired him in brotherhood with Khabbāb ibn al-Aratt.
He witnessed Badr and the other battles, and the banner of the Banū Muʿāwiyah ibn Mālik was entrusted to him on the day of the Conquest (1).
al-Wāqidī, Ibn Saʿd, Khalīfah, Ibn Zabr (2), and Ibn Mandah said: He died in the year 61.
It is said: He lived 91 years.
And in al-Muwaṭṭaʾ: عن عبد الله بن عبد الله بن جابر بن عتيك، عن جده لأمه عتيك بن الحارث، قال:
Jābir ibn ʿAtīk informed me:
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to visit ⟦2:36⟧ ʿAbd Allāh ibn Thābit, and found that he had been overcome, so he said "to Allah we belong and to Him we return", and said: We have been overcome concerning you (1).
I say: The correct view is that Jābir ibn ʿAtīk is the subject of this report and of the report of the date of death, and that Jabr died early, and that Jābir was of the Banū Ghanm ibn Salamah, and Allah knows best.
Their paternal uncle was al-Ḥārith ibn Qays ibn Hayshah al-Awsī (2).
A distinguished Badrī (البدري), counted by: al-Wāqidī and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUmārah.
Ibn ʿUqbah did not mention him, nor did Ibn Isḥāq or Abū Maʿshar; rather Ibn Isḥāq and Abū Maʿshar said: Jabr ibn ʿAtīk ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Qays ibn Hayshah.
